```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

InsectTrack turns videos of insects into tracks and activity measures. A
video is read frame by frame, insects are detected in every analysed frame,
detections are linked into tracks, and the tracks are summarised as counts,
activity time series, heat maps and hot spots, visits to regions such as
flowers, insects entering and leaving nests and hives, and proximity
interactions. An annotated video shows every insect with its own colour and
identity label.

A track is the record of one insect while it stays in view. An insect that
leaves the field of view and returns starts a new track, so the number of
tracks is not the number of individuals.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("ehsanrahimi666/InsectTrack")
```

Detection with deep-learning models (YOLO, Grounding DINO, OWLv2, OWL-ViT),
segmentation with SAM 2.1 and the BoxMOT trackers run in Python through
'reticulate'. `it_install_backend()` creates a virtual environment with the
required modules; `it_backend_status()` reports the module versions and the
device (`cuda`, `mps` or `cpu`) that will be used.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(InsectTrack)
it_install_backend()                 # once; it_install_backend(gpu = TRUE) for an NVIDIA GPU
reticulate::use_virtualenv("insecttrack")
it_backend_status()
```

Background subtraction, the trackers implemented in R (Hungarian assignment,
SORT and ByteTrack), all summaries, figures, the annotated video and the
evaluation metrics need no Python.

## One call per video

`it_track_video()` runs the whole analysis and writes the results to a
folder: the annotated video, tables (`detections.csv`, `tracks.csv`,
`track_summary.csv`, `activity.csv`, `heatmap.csv`, and, when requested,
`entrance_events.csv`, `entrance_counts.csv`, `visits.csv`,
`line_crossings.csv`, `interactions.csv`), figures (trajectories, heat map,
hot spots, activity, entrance traffic), `settings.json` with all settings and
software versions, and `report.html`. Any format that FFmpeg reads can be
used, including smartphone videos with a rotation flag.

Honeybees on flowers, with a YOLO model trained on annotated frames of the
study system and flower outlines as regions of interest:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- it_track_video("delosperma.mp4", detector = "yolo", model = "bees_yolo.pt",
                      detector_args = list(imgsz = 1280), fps = 10,
                      rois = it_read_rois_json("flowers.json"), output_dir = "results/delosperma")
res
```

A hive entrance without a trained model: Grounding DINO finds the bees from a
text prompt, and the entrance is located from the end points of the tracks
(`entrance = "auto"`) or given as a polygon. Several prompts can be given;
the one with the highest scores on a few frames is used.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- it_track_video("hive.mp4", detector = "gdino", prompt = c("bee", "honeybee"),
                      fps = 5, duration = 60, entrance = "auto", output_dir = "results/hive")
res$entrance$counts      # insects in and out per time bin
```

A laboratory arena with a plain background, where background subtraction is
sufficient and fast:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- it_track_video("arena.mp4", detector = "motion", fps = 25, interaction_dist = 60,
                      detector_args = list(min_area = 20), output_dir = "results/arena")
```

`it_track_videos()` processes several videos with the same settings and
returns one summary row per video.

## Choosing a detector

* A **YOLO model trained on frames of the study system** is the most
  accurate and fastest option (about 0.1-0.3 s per frame on a CPU, much less
  on a GPU). Models do not transfer well between scenes: a model trained on
  small bees on flowers may miss bees filmed close up at a hive entrance.
* **Grounding DINO** (`detector = "gdino"`) and **OWLv2 or OWL-ViT**
  (`detector = "owl"`) detect insects described by a text prompt without
  training. They take several seconds per frame on a CPU and miss many small
  insects, so they are best used on a GPU, at a reduced frame rate, or to
  pre-label frames for annotation.
* **Background subtraction** (`detector = "motion"`) needs a fixed camera
  and a plain background; outdoors, moving leaves, flowers and shadows cause
  many false detections.

## From pre-labels to a trained model

`it_prelabel()` samples frames, detects insects with Grounding DINO, refines
the boxes with SAM 2.1 and writes images and labels that CVAT, Label Studio
or Roboflow import. After correction, the labels train a YOLO model with
'Ultralytics', which is then passed to `it_track_video()` as `model`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
it_prelabel("hive.mp4", out_dir = "prelabels", n = 200, prompt = "bee")
# correct the boxes in an annotation tool, then in Python:
#   from ultralytics import YOLO
#   YOLO("yolo26n.pt").train(data = "bees.yaml", imgsz = 1280, epochs = 100)
```

## Example: honeybees on flowers

The package contains a 10-s video of honeybees visiting *Delosperma* flowers
(`it_example_video()`) and the detections of this video by a YOLO26n bee
detector (`it_example_detections()`), so that the steps after detection can
be run without Python.

```{r example-tracks, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
library(InsectTrack)
v   <- it_example_video()
it_video_info(v)
det <- it_example_detections()
tr  <- it_track(det, "bytetrack", track_thresh = 0.25, new_track_thresh = 0.3, frame_rate = 10)
fr  <- it_extract_frames(v, gray = FALSE)
bg  <- it_read_frame(fr$file[50], gray = FALSE)
it_plot_tracks(tr, 640, 360, background = bg)
```

```{r example-summary, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
s <- it_track_summary(tr, width = 640, height = 360)
s[, c("track", "n", "duration", "path_length", "mean_speed")]
hm <- it_hotspots(it_heatmap(tr, 640, 360, cell = 16, frames = fr, smooth = 1))
it_plot_heatmap(hm, background = bg)
```

The annotated video is written with

```{r, eval = FALSE}
it_render_video(fr, tr, "honeybees_tracked.mp4")
```

Tracked frames of other insects, with the sources and licences of their
videos, are listed by `it_example_gallery()`.

## Step by step

The steps of `it_track_video()` are available as separate functions.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fr  <- it_extract_frames("hive.mp4", fps = 10, width = 1280, gray = FALSE, format = "png")
det <- it_detect_gdino(fr, prompt = "bee")
tr  <- it_track(det, method = "bytetrack", frame_rate = 10)
tr  <- it_stitch(tr, max_gap = 1, max_dist = 60)
hm  <- it_hotspots(it_heatmap(tr, 1280, 720, cell = 20, frames = fr))
zone <- it_find_entrance(tr, 1280, 720)
ec  <- it_entrance_counts(tr, zone, bin = 10, frames = fr)
it_render_video(fr, tr, "hive_tracked.mp4", entrance = zone, events = ec$events)
```

The example below runs without Python on a small synthetic video with two
moving squares.

```{r}
library(InsectTrack)
dir <- tempfile("synthetic_"); dir.create(dir)
for (k in 1:30) {
  m <- array(0.9, c(120, 160, 3))
  m[40 + 0:5, 20 + 3 * k + 0:5, ] <- 0.1
  m[80 + 0:5, 140 - 2 * k + 0:5, ] <- 0.1
  png::writePNG(m, file.path(dir, sprintf("img_%03d.png", k)))
}
video <- file.path(dir, "synthetic.mp4")
av::av_encode_video(list.files(dir, "\\.png$", full.names = TRUE), video, framerate = 10, verbose = FALSE)
res <- it_track_video(video, output_dir = file.path(dir, "out"), detector = "motion", fps = 10,
                      detector_args = list(min_area = 10, bg_frames = 15), verbose = FALSE)
res
head(res$track_summary[, c("track", "n", "duration", "path_length", "mean_speed")])
```

## Accuracy against annotations

Detections and tracks can be compared with annotated frames:
`it_eval_detections()` (precision, recall and F1, matching by distance or
box overlap), `it_eval_tracks()` (CLEAR MOT and IDF1) and `it_eval_hota()`
(HOTA with its detection, association and localisation components;
`it_combine_hota()` pools sequences).

```{r}
g <- data.frame(frame = 1:20, x = 1:20 * 3, y = 40, id = 1, width = 8, height = 8)
p <- transform(g, track = ifelse(frame <= 10, 1, 2))  # one insect split into two tracks
it_eval_hota(p, g)[, c("hota", "deta", "assa")]
it_eval_tracks(p, g, max_dist = 5)[, c("mota", "idf1", "id_switches")]
```
